deepdive.thesis: Whirlpool India delivered a strong turnaround with 17% revenue growth and 100% PBT growth in 9M FY25, driven by triple-digit market share gains across refrigerators and washers, alongside 220 bps gross margin expansion — what matters is the sustainable, ROI-backed execution and impending strategic autonomy post-30% sell-down, which unlocks faster investment decisions and potential margin expansion beyond current e-waste distortions.

drhp.business: Whirlpool of India manufactures and distributes consumer durable goods - refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, microwave ovens and other home appliances - for households across a wide range of income levels. The Company serves the Indian market through a pan-India omni-channel network spanning traditional retail, modern trade, e-commerce and other distribution outlets, and also exports to select international markets.
drhp.end_markets: Pan-India - 28 States and 7 Union Territories|International - 11 countries (exports ~3% of total turnover)
drhp.expansion: Whirlpool operates three manufacturing facilities in India - Pune (Direct Cool and No Frost refrigerators), Faridabad (Direct Cool refrigerators) and Puducherry (Semi-automatic, Fully-automatic and Front-load washing machines). The Company began manufacturing front-load washing machines in India in the second half of 2022, widening its product portfolio beyond the historically manufactured direct-cool refrigerators and semi-automatic washing machines. No new capacity addition, plant commissioning or expansion project for FY2025-26 is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.note: Following the January 30, 2025 announcement of Whirlpool Corporation's Anticipated Sell-Down, the Company constituted a Transition Committee (with legal counsel AZB & Partners) and executed a Brand License Agreement and Technology License Agreement with Promoter Group entities on October 16, 2025; the dilution of the Promoter's shareholding introduces structural uncertainty even though management currently expects no material long-term operational impact
risks.risk: Promoter transition / Whirlpool Corporation's Anticipated Sell-Down

risks.note: IT infrastructure currently relies on Transition Services Agreements (TSA) with the Promoter Group following the sell-down; seamless transition of IT systems/applications after TSA expiry remains an unresolved risk, with a roadmap being developed via an external consultant
Post-transition, brand name, IP, engineering, innovation pipeline and product development support depend on the Technology License Agreement with Whirlpool Corporation rather than in-house ownership

The transitionary phase heightens risk of losing key executives and senior management; the Board approved the Whirlpool of India Employee Stock Option Plan 2026 (subject to shareholder approval) to mitigate attrition risk
risks.risk: Talent acquisition and retention during transition

risks.note: New and expanding manufacturers in the consumer durables sector intensify competitive pressure, requiring continued investment in innovation, pricing and geographic reach to defend market position
Complex and evolving regulatory landscape (energy norms, Compressor BIS requirements) may require production/product changes or high-cost compliance investment
Geopolitical developments (including the Middle East conflict) have disrupted the supply chain, raising input costs and limiting availability of input materials, posing operational and financial risk
